questions.prompt: A proof that the diagonals of parallelogram ABCD bisect each other (they meet at E): 1. AB = CD  (?) 2. ∠BAE ≅ ∠DCE  (?) 3. ∠AEB ≅ ∠CED  (?) 4. △ABE ≅ △CDE  (?) 5. AE = CE, BE = DE  (?) Give the five reasons.
questions.prompt_markup:
A proof that the diagonals of parallelogram ABCD bisect each other (they meet at E):
1. AB = CD  (?)
2. ∠BAE ≅ ∠DCE  (?)
3. ∠AEB ≅ ∠CED  (?)
4. △ABE ≅ △CDE  (?)
5. AE = CE, BE = DE  (?)
Give the five reasons.
questions.correct_answer: 1: opposite sides of a parallelogram are congruent; 2: alternate interior angles (AB ∥ DC); 3: vertical angles; 4: AAS; 5: corresponding parts.
questions.grading_note: Any equivalent names for all five reasons.

questions.skill: Prove that a 180° rotation carries a parallelogram onto itself
questions.standard_level: Geometry. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Geometry, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.response: write the answer and show the required work
questions.prompt: ABCD is a parallelogram whose diagonals meet at E. Prove that the 180° rotation about E maps ABCD onto itself.
questions.prompt_markup: ABCD is a parallelogram whose diagonals meet at E. Prove that the 180° rotation about E maps ABCD onto itself.
questions.correct_answer: A ↔ C and B ↔ D, so the parallelogram maps onto itself.
questions.required_method: Use the fact that E is the midpoint of both diagonals to find the images of the vertices.
questions.grading_note: Any valid proof (paragraph, two-column, or flow). Essential: a 180° rotation about E maps each point P to the point P′ with E the midpoint of PP′; E is the midpoint of AC and BD, so A → C, C → A, B → D, D → B; segments map to segments, so each side maps onto its opposite side.
